title: Cursor AI Pricing 2026: Free Plan Limits and Features
summary: The cursor free plan provides access to core code editing tools while restricting advanced AI agent features and deep repository indexing.
body_markdown:
## Cursor pricing and plan limits for 2026


### Hobby (Free) plan limits


**2,000 completions per month** is the ceiling for the Hobby tier. This low limit means you'll likely exhaust your quota within two days of active coding, forcing a transition to manual typing. This tier doesn't have "fast" requests.


When you interact with a high-reasoning model like GPT-6 Astra, you are subject to a[slow queue](https://fast.io/resources/cursor-fast-requests/) that can delay responses by **20 to 60 seconds** during peak hours.


### Pro plan features and cost


At $20 per month, the Pro plan is the entry point for frontier models like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, meaning users must commit to a recurring subscription to access the latest AI capabilities. Cursor's analysis puts the monthly fast request count at 500.


This ensures that complex refactoring tasks happen in seconds rather than minutes.


Pricing that scales with granularity often penalizes the precise engineering required for stable automation, effectively taxing the builder for decomposing work into reliable, smaller steps.


Activepieces addresses this by making the run the meter, so a ten-step process costs the same to run as the two-step workaround it replaced.


One credit is charged per flow run regardless of how the flow is built, allowing teams to enforce per-project cost caps while maintaining the granular discipline good automation depends on.


This allows teams to build complex DevOps pipelines without the per-task cost overhead found on the Make or Zapier pricing pages.


### Business plan for teams


**$40 per user** is the price for the Business plan, which is the only tier that includes centralized billing and administrative controls for growing startups.


Companies must pay a premium to manage team access and expenses efficiently. Its primary value is the enforcement of Privacy Mode by default.


By enabling this setting, you ensure that proprietary code isn't ever used for training the underlying models. Without this, a company risks leaking intellectual property into the public training sets of future model iterations.


### Comparison of usage quotas and model access


The following table breaks down the 2026 service levels to show how request volume and privacy protections scale across the subscription tiers.


Plan Monthly Price Fast Requests Codebase Indexing Privacy Mode


Hobby $0 0 Limited Optional


Pro $20 500 Full Optional


Pro+ $40 1,000 Full Optional


Ultra $90 2,500 Full Included


Teams $40/user 500/user Full Included


This structure forces a choice between immediate performance and long-term cost, as the "slow queue" on the Hobby tier effectively prevents the use of AI for real-time pair programming.


On the Hobby tier, moving to a paid tier is the only way to maintain a fluid development velocity.
